standard_prerequisites.name: Existence of finite limits and colimits in an abelian category
standard_prerequisites.use: Supplies the existence of finite limits and colimits and the construction of kernels and cokernels from equalizers and coequalizers.

standard_prerequisites.name: Exactness of adjoint functors
standard_prerequisites.use: Shows that the left exact left adjoint is exact and that the right adjoint is left exact.

core_obligations: Kernels and cokernels (proof lines 1892-1915): the left adjoint is exact, so it preserves kernels and cokernels; since every morphism of the source category is the image of a morphism under the composite, the author concludes that kernels and cokernels exist and identifies them with the images of the kernels and cokernels computed in the abelian category.
The canonical comparison (proof lines 1916-1923): having kernels and cokernels, the category has finite limits and colimits, so the right adjoint is left exact and preserves kernels.

Conclusion (proof lines 1924-1957): the author computes the coimage and the image of a morphism using the identifications obtained, compares them, and concludes that the canonical map between them is an isomorphism, which is the remaining axiom for the category to be abelian.
proof_roadmap: Use exactness of the left adjoint to transfer kernels and cokernels.
Use the existence of kernels and cokernels to get finite limits and colimits and exactness of the right adjoint.
Compare the coimage and the image of a morphism to conclude.
difficulty_reason: The lemma states that an additive category carrying an additive right adjoint which is left exact into an abelian category, whose composite with that adjoint is isomorphic to the identity, is itself abelian (statement lines 1878-1889). The proof is a complete argument: exactness of the left adjoint transfers kernels and cokernels from the abelian category, using that every morphism of the source arises under the composite (proof lines 1892-1915); the resulting existence of finite limits and colimits makes the right adjoint left exact (proof lines 1916-1923); and the author compares the coimage and the image of a morphism, expressed through the transferred kernels and cokernels, to obtain the last axiom (proof lines 1924-1957). The non-formal content is the transfer of kernels and cokernels and the comparison of coimage and image. The claim is H2: a structured argument with each input named.
